done_when: Reproduce it (run the two tests in a loop under load on macOS), name the root cause with evidence, fix it at the cause so forge work never returns while a Codex process it started is alive, and both tests pass on every OS in CI three runs in a row; no test is skipped or loosened

findings.body: The loop falls through after five seconds even if every process-group probe succeeds. If termination is still pending, Forge returns while its app-server remains alive. The later cleanup cannot close this gap in the bare-command scenario: src/forge/codex.py:365-368 skips that app-server record, including when invoked by hold() at line 416. Confirm termination before returning instead of treating exhaustion of the polling budget as completion.

findings.body: On Windows this test finishes after fixture setup without starting the worker, killing its driver, or checking that the app-server exited. It therefore reports success even if its named lifecycle behavior is broken. This violates the explicit test-audit and no-skipped-tests requirements. Exercise the lifecycle scenario on Windows with an appropriate process-query fixture and retain the immediate post-return assertion.
